clue.text: Without being expected, forcing gruff exterior

indicators.note: an exterior is the outer layer of something, so the word for gruff becomes the shell around the other word

parts.note: gruff = bad-tempered and curt; its letters form the outside
forcing open with a lever; this word goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone is caught off guard by a person forcing a gruff front.
explanation.walkthrough: Prising is the British spelling of prying (forcing something open with a lever).
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrase: an adverb for something happening in a way nobody expected.

clue.text: Herb is wise

definitions.meaning: a grey-green kitchen herb often paired with onion in stuffing
an adjective for someone full of wisdom, also a noun for a wise person

explanation.surface: A claim that some herb has wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: Two unrelated meanings of one word, joined by 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both: a culinary plant by name, and a formal adjective for wisdom.

clue.text: Arrived and delivered a sermon — not quietly!

indicators.note: 'not quietly' means without the quiet, so the letter standing for quietly is taken away

parts.note: what a minister did from the pulpit
p (piano) is the musical mark for quietly; it is removed

explanation.surface: A preacher turns up and gives a loud sermon.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the P from the sermon word leaves a synonym for arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: to get to a destination.

clue.text: Again take up weapons behind male

parts.note: the noun: one's backside or the back part
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: A man arms himself once more, standing behind another man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a position word, but here it is a noun meaning backside.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym phrase: the RE- prefix supplies 'again' and ARM supplies 'take up weapons'.

clue.text: Interference in stable

definitions.meaning: the crackle that disturbs a radio or TV signal

explanation.surface: Some disturbance going on in a horse's stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable' suggests horses; it is the adjective meaning steady.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both: the noun for electrical crackle and the adjective for things that stay put.

clue.text: The French return after no time with token

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so the French article is read backwards

parts.note: used as it stands
MIN is short for minute, a unit of time

indicators.note: the reversed article comes after the other pieces in the answer

parts.note: la is French for 'the' (feminine)

explanation.surface: French visitors head home after a quick trip, taking a souvenir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Token' looks like a noun (a coin or souvenir); it is the adjective, as in a token gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as adjectives: a payment in name only, like a token fee.

clue.text: Line on foremost tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, one thing placed on another sits above it, so the line letter comes first

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line
chief or principal, as in archenemy or arch rival

explanation.surface: A line is drawn on the tree at the front of the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foremost' reads as a position; it is the adjective meaning chief.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a deciduous conifer, one kind of tree.

clue.text: Edge inside relatives' footwear

indicators.note: the edge is placed inside the relatives, so their word wraps round it

parts.note: male offspring, family members
the rim or brim of a cup or crater

explanation.surface: Someone finds an edge tucked inside the shoes belonging to family members.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe on 'relatives' is surface dressing; the wordplay just wants a word for relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: laceless shoes you push your feet into are one kind of footwear.

clue.text: Hang out round a country in Africa

indicators.note: letters that are out of place are disordered, so HANG and A are rearranged

parts.note: used as it stands, to be rearranged
used as it stands

explanation.surface: An invitation to hang out around an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hang out' reads as a phrase meaning to relax; 'out' is the rearranging instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a West African nation whose capital is Accra.

clue.text: Almost respect a lost naval officer

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the synonym for respect loses its last letter

parts.note: respect = admire, minus its final E
used as it stands
the first letter of lost, as used for defeats in sports league tables

explanation.surface: Some grudging regard for a naval officer who has gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: L for lost comes from win/lose/draw columns in sports results.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the highest rank of commander in a navy.

clue.text: Making no mishap during golf shot at sporting contest

indicators.note: making something means forming it from raw material, so the letters of 'no mishap' are formed into something new

parts.note: a short lofted shot onto the green

indicators.note: one thing happening during another sits within it, so the rearranged letters go inside the golf shot

parts.note: the letters of 'no mishap' rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer plays a clean chip shot at a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making no mishap' reads as playing without error; 'Making' is the rearranging instruction and 'no mishap' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a competition held to decide the title holder in a sport.

clue.text: Bright lick of paint for former British soldier

parts.note: a vivid colour
a lick of paint is a single layer

explanation.surface: A bright coat of paint to spruce up an old soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The nickname for British soldiers of the 17th to 19th centuries came from their scarlet tunics.
explanation.definitionFit: A historical nickname: British infantry of past centuries, named for their uniforms.

clue.text: Shipyard workers head off with senior people

indicators.note: a head taken off leaves the body, so the first letter of the workers' word is removed

parts.note: people who join steel plates in a shipyard; the W goes

explanation.surface: Shipyard workers leave, accompanied by their seniors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head off' looks like workers going somewhere; it removes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: older people, or those holding senior standing in a community or church.

clue.text: Background talk of edible stalks

definitions.meaning: the meaningless word stage crowds mutter to sound like chatter
pink sour stems cooked in crumbles and pies

explanation.surface: A chat about vegetable stems.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage the plant's name also means meaningless chatter, from stage crowds repeating the word.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both: a British idiom for murmured noise, and the plant grown for its tart stalks.

clue.text: Points to follow excess of protein

indicators.note: to follow is to come after, so the points go after the word for excess

parts.note: an oversupply
E and N are compass points

explanation.surface: Advice about what comes after eating too much protein.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points (N, E, S, W) are a standard source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the protein in wheat that makes dough elastic.

clue.text: Dull replacement in trash

indicators.note: replacement means putting things back in different places, so the letters take new positions

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boring replacement part ends up in the bin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to take the shine off metal, or a reputation.

clue.text: I'd oust again from TV room?

indicators.note: doing something again means making it anew, so the letters are put together afresh in a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A presenter vows to throw someone out of the television set once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Again' reads as a repeat of the ousting; it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the room where television programmes are recorded.

clue.text: Track to accommodate electrical component

parts.note: a racing track, a loop for motor racing
to take in lodgers and feed them

explanation.surface: Instructions to lay a track that will fit an electrical part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To accommodate' sounds like an instruction to put one piece inside another; it means to house lodgers.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the printed panel carrying the wiring in electronic devices.

clue.text: Resist rise of social outcast

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that rises goes upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: someone shunned, originally for disease

explanation.surface: Opposing the social climb of someone shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rise' reads as the outcast's social climb; it turns the word upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: to fight off or hold back an attack.

clue.text: Fresh air to circle area

parts.note: the letter shaped like a circle
a region or district

explanation.surface: Fresh air being pumped around a region.
explanation.walkthrough: The gas's name is also jokey British slang for bracing seaside air.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional informal sense: in Britain the gas's name is used for invigorating air, especially at the seaside.

clue.text: Selfish person contrived ruse

indicators.note: contrived means artificially arranged, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A selfish person cooked up a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrived' reads as the verb of the sentence; it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who exploits others for their own ends.

clue.text: To show that you like iPhone program, double back

parts.note: the short name for a phone application

indicators.note: going back means going in the opposite direction, so the word for double is read backwards

parts.note: twofold, reversed to LAUD

explanation.surface: To like an iPhone app, tap twice to go back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double back' looks like one phrase meaning return; 'double' is a word for twofold and 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive phrase for clapping or praising: showing approval of something you like.

clue.text: Neglects section of ballroom, it seems

indicators.note: a section is a part cut from a whole, so the answer is a run of letters cut from the following words

parts.note: the letters run from the end of ballroom across 'it' into the start of seems

explanation.surface: Someone apparently ignores part of the ballroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma is surface punctuation; letters run across it.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym as verbs: leaves out or fails to attend to.

clue.text: Stick as one to pool resources

parts.note: a heavy stick used as a weapon
in unison, jointly

explanation.surface: An urging to stay united and share what you have.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a verb (stick together); it is the noun for a cudgel.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: to combine money with others for a shared purchase.
